title: Microsoft Word
tagline: Write clear, professional documents, with practice in every module
summary: Learn to produce documents people want to read: formatting, structure with styles, tables, letters, résumés, reports, proofreading and sharing. Every module has a document lab that checks your work.

modules.title: Start a document
modules.summary: Find your way around a word processor, type and edit with confidence, and save files so you can always find them.
modules.outcome: You can create a document, select and edit text quickly, use undo and find and replace, and save it in the right format with a sensible name.
modules.intro: Most written work today begins in a word processor. Microsoft Word, Google Docs and LibreOffice Writer all share the same ideas, so what you learn here works in all of them. This module covers the basics that save the most time: moving around, editing quickly and saving safely.

topics.title: The parts of a word processor
topics.html:
A word processor has a few areas that are always there. Knowing where each one is makes every other lesson easier.

The main areas
AreaWhat it is for
Page (or canvas)Where you type; it shows how the printed page will look
Toolbar or ribbonButtons for formatting, inserting and reviewing
Menu or tabsGroups of commands: Home, Insert, Layout, Review, View
Status barPage number, word count and zoom
RulerShows margins and indents

The cursor is the blinking line that shows where your next letter will appear. Click in the text to move it, or use the arrow keys. The selection is the text you have highlighted; most formatting applies to the selection.

Tip

The word count in the status bar is useful for school work and for applications that give a limit, such as 250 words.

Try it yourself: If you type but nothing appears where you expected, what should you check first?

Model answer. Where the cursor is. Click where you want to type, and check that no other text is selected, because typing replaces a selection.

Check what you just learned

1. What does the blinking line in a document show?
  • The page number
  • The margin
  • Where the next letter will appear (correct)
  • A spelling error

It is the cursor, the insertion point for typing.

2. Typing while text is selected will:
  • Add to it
  • Do nothing
  • Format it
  • Replace the selected text (correct)

Typing replaces whatever is highlighted.
keyPoints: The page, toolbar, tabs, status bar and ruler are always there.
The cursor shows where text will appear; the selection is what formatting changes.
The status bar shows the word count.

topics.title: Typing, selecting and editing quickly
topics.html:
Good editing is mostly about selecting the right amount of text and acting on it. A few mouse and keyboard habits do most of the work.

Selecting text
To selectDo this
A wordDouble-click it
A paragraphTriple-click it
EverythingCtrl+A (Cmd+A on a Mac)
A stretch of textClick at the start, hold Shift, click at the end
Shortcuts worth learning
ShortcutDoes
Ctrl+CCopy
Ctrl+XCut
Ctrl+VPaste
Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+YUndo / Redo
Ctrl+FFind a word
Ctrl+B / I / UBold / Italic / Underline
Worked example

Find and replace

You wrote 'Mr. Sharma' twelve times but it should be 'Mr Sharma'.

  1. Open Find and Replace (Ctrl+H).
  2. Find: Mr. Sharma. Replace with: Mr Sharma.
  3. Choose Replace All and check the count.

Answer. Find and replace fixes every occurrence at once. Always glance through the result to be sure nothing unexpected changed.

Watch out

Be careful with Replace All: replacing 'the' also changes 'other' and 'mother'. Use whole word matching when available.

Common mistakes

  • Pressing Enter at the end of every line: let the text wrap by itself and press Enter only to start a new paragraph.
  • Using spaces to move text across the page: use alignment, tabs or a table instead.

Check what you just learned

1. How do you select one whole paragraph?
  • Triple-click it (correct)
  • Click once
  • Press Ctrl+B
  • Press Esc

A triple-click selects the whole paragraph.

2. When should you press Enter?
  • At the end of every line
  • To start a new paragraph (correct)
  • To go to the next page
  • To make text bigger

Text wraps by itself; Enter starts a new paragraph.

3. Which shortcut undoes your last action?
  • Ctrl+P
  • Ctrl+U
  • Ctrl+Z (correct)
  • Ctrl+K

Ctrl+Z is Undo.
keyPoints: Double-click selects a word, triple-click a paragraph.
Copy, cut, paste and undo are Ctrl+C, X, V and Z.
Press Enter only to start a new paragraph.

topics.title: Saving, naming and file formats
topics.html:
Save early and often. A good file name saves hours later: choose a name that says what the file is, with the date or version if it will change, such as science-report-v2.docx. Avoid names like final-final2.

Common formats
FormatBest for
DOCX (Word)Documents you or others will still edit
PDFFinished documents that must look the same everywhere
TXT (plain text)Very simple text with no formatting
ODTThe open format of LibreOffice
Tip

Cloud tools such as Google Docs and OneDrive save automatically and keep a version history, so you can go back to yesterday's version.

Watch out

Send a PDF, not the editable file, when you do not want anyone to change your document.

Check what you just learned

1. Which format keeps a finished document looking the same on any device?
  • TXT
  • ODT
  • DOCX
  • PDF (correct)

PDF fixes the layout.

2. Which file name is best?
  • science-report-v2.docx (correct)
  • final
  • doc1
  • new new

It says what it is and which version.

Key terms: flip and sort

Cursor
The blinking line where typing appears
Selection
Highlighted text that commands act on
Undo
Takes back the last action (Ctrl+Z)
DOCX
The standard editable Word format
PDF
A fixed-layout format for finished documents
keyPoints: Save early, often and with a clear name.
DOCX for editing, PDF for sending finished work.

modules.title: Format text and paragraphs
modules.summary: Choose fonts, sizes, alignment, spacing and lists so a page is easy to read.
modules.outcome: You can format text and paragraphs consistently, use lists properly and avoid the mistakes that make documents look messy.
modules.intro: Good formatting is invisible: the reader simply finds the page easy to read. This module teaches the handful of choices that matter most, and a few habits that keep a document consistent.

topics.title: Fonts, size and emphasis
topics.html:
A font (typeface) is the style of the letters. Choose one clear font for body text, and at most one more for headings. Body text between 10 and 12 points reads comfortably on paper and screen.

Choosing type
ChoiceGood habit
FontOne or two per document; avoid decorative fonts for long text
Size11 or 12 point for body, larger for headings
BoldFor key words and headings, sparingly
ItalicFor titles of books, foreign words and light emphasis
UnderlineAvoid: it looks like a link
ColourDark text on a light background; never rely on colour alone
Watch out

If everything is bold, nothing stands out. Use emphasis for the few things the reader must not miss.

Try it yourself: Why is underlining a poor way to emphasise text on a screen?

Model answer. People expect underlined text to be a link, so it can confuse readers; use bold instead.

Check what you just learned

1. What is a sensible size for body text?
  • 6 points
  • 11 or 12 points (correct)
  • 30 points
  • 48 points

Eleven or twelve points is comfortable.

2. Why avoid underlining for emphasis?
  • It uses ink
  • It is banned
  • It looks like a link (correct)
  • It changes the font

Underlined text on screens suggests a link.
keyPoints: One or two fonts; body text 11 to 12 points.
Use bold sparingly and avoid underlining for emphasis.
Contrast matters: dark text on a light background.

topics.title: Alignment, spacing and indents
topics.html:
Alignment
AlignmentUse for
LeftBody text: the easiest to read
CentreTitles, short notices, invitations
RightDates or addresses in a letter header
JustifiedNewspaper-style columns; can leave uneven gaps in narrow text

Line spacing (1.0 to 2.0) controls how tightly lines sit. 1.15 or 1.5 is comfortable for most reading. Space before and after a paragraph adds a gap between paragraphs, which is better than pressing Enter to make blank lines.

An indent moves a paragraph in from the margin. A first-line indent marks a new paragraph in long text; a hanging indent is used in bibliographies where the first line is out and the rest are in.

Tip

To change the gap between paragraphs for the whole document, change the paragraph spacing setting once instead of adding blank lines.

Common mistakes

  • Centring long paragraphs: they become hard to read.
  • Using the space bar or Tab several times to indent.
  • Different spacing in different paragraphs.

Check what you just learned

1. Which alignment is easiest to read for long text?
  • Centre
  • None
  • Right
  • Left (correct)

Left alignment keeps a steady starting edge.

2. How should you add space between paragraphs?
  • Set space after the paragraph (correct)
  • Press Enter twice
  • Press Tab
  • Add dots

Paragraph spacing is part of the format.
keyPoints: Left-align body text and centre only short lines.
Use paragraph spacing, not blank lines.
Indents are set with indent controls, not spaces.

topics.title: Bulleted and numbered lists
topics.html:
A list breaks a long sentence into short items. Use bullets when order does not matter and numbers when it does, such as steps in a process.

Bullets or numbers
SituationChoose
Things to pack for a tripBullets
Steps to log in to a websiteNumbers
Four benefits of exerciseBullets
Ranking the top five booksNumbers

Writing good list items

  1. Start each item the same way (all verbs, or all nouns).
  2. Keep items short, ideally one line.
  3. Do not mix full sentences and fragments.
  4. Use real list buttons so spacing and numbering stay correct.
Worked example

Fix a list

A student wrote: To bake bread you need flour, and water, you should add yeast, salt.

  1. Break it into items: flour, water, yeast, salt.
  2. Use bullets because the order does not matter.
  3. Start with a lead line: To bake bread you need:

Answer. A list with a short lead line and parallel items is easier to scan than a long sentence.

Check what you just learned

1. Which needs a numbered list?
  • Items to buy
  • Steps to reset a password (correct)
  • Colours you like
  • Names of friends

Steps happen in order.

2. Why use the list button instead of typing a dash?
  • It is faster only
  • Dashes are banned
  • It keeps spacing and numbering correct when you edit (correct)
  • It changes the font

A real list adjusts itself.

Key terms: flip and sort

Font
The style of the letters
Point
The unit for text size
Line spacing
The gap between lines
Indent
Moving a paragraph in from the margin
Bullet list
Items where order does not matter
Numbered list
Items in a sequence
keyPoints: Bullets when order does not matter, numbers when it does.
Keep items short and in the same pattern.

questions.explanation: Too many fonts distract the reader.

questions.text: Justified text can cause:
questions.explanation: Spaces are stretched to fill the line.

questions.text: A hanging indent is common in:
questions.explanation: The first line is out and the rest are in.

questions.text: For steps in a process you should use:
questions.explanation: Order matters, so number the steps.

questions.text: Which line spacing is comfortable for reading?
Underlining plain text on a screen suggests:

modules.title: Structure with styles
modules.summary: Use heading styles, page setup, headers, footers and page numbers to turn a pile of text into a navigable document.
modules.outcome: You can structure a long document with heading styles, set margins and orientation, and add page numbers and headers.
modules.intro: A long document without structure is a wall of text. Styles are the single most useful feature in a word processor: they give every title and paragraph its role, so the document can be restyled, navigated and given a contents list automatically.

topics.title: Headings and styles
topics.html:
Definition

Style. A saved set of formatting (font, size, spacing, colour) with a name, such as Heading 1 or Normal, that you apply to a paragraph in one click.

A typical heading structure
LevelUsed forExample
Title / Heading 1The document titleWater Use at Our School
Heading 2Main sectionsFindings
Heading 3SubsectionsTaps and toilets
NormalBody textThe paragraphs themselves

When you use heading styles, the word processor knows the outline of your document. You can jump between sections in the navigation pane, and generate a table of contents with one click.

Watch out

Making a title big and bold by hand looks the same, but the document does not know it is a heading, so navigation and contents lists do not work.

Common mistakes

  • Skipping levels, such as a Heading 3 straight under a Heading 1.
  • Using more than one Heading 1 in a short report.
  • Formatting headings by hand.

Check what you just learned

1. What is the main benefit of heading styles?
  • They are prettier
  • They add colour
  • They shorten text
  • The document gets a structure that tools can use (correct)

Styles give the document an outline.

2. Which is the correct order of headings?
  • Heading 1, 2, 3 (correct)
  • Heading 3, 1, 2
  • Heading 2, 3, 1
  • Any order

Levels go from main to detail.
keyPoints: Use Heading 1, 2 and 3 for structure, Normal for body text.
Styles update everything at once and power the navigation pane and contents list.

topics.title: Page setup: margins, orientation and size
topics.html:
Page setup choices
SettingTypical choiceWhy
Paper sizeA4 (India, UK) or Letter (US)Match the printer and the audience
Margins2.5 cm or 1 inch all roundLeaves room for binding and handling
OrientationPortrait for text, landscape for wide tablesChoose what fits the content
ColumnsOne for reports, two or three for newslettersShort lines are easier to scan
Tip

Set the page up before you start typing. Changing paper size late can shift tables and pictures.

Worked example

A wide table

A timetable has eight columns and does not fit on a portrait page.

  1. Change the page orientation to landscape.
  2. Or reduce the font size slightly in the table.
  3. Or split the table into two.

Answer. Choose the layout that keeps the content readable: landscape is often the simplest fix for wide tables.

Check what you just learned

1. When is landscape orientation useful?
  • For long essays
  • For wide tables (correct)
  • For letters
  • Never

More width helps wide tables.
keyPoints: Choose paper size and margins first.
Landscape suits wide tables.

topics.title: Headers, footers and page numbers
topics.html:
A header is the area at the top of every page; a footer is the area at the bottom. They hold things that repeat: the document title, your name, the date or a page number.

What to put where

  • Header: short title or chapter name.
  • Footer: page number, in the form 'Page 2 of 5'.
  • First page: often no header; the title page speaks for itself.

Page numbers are inserted as a field, not typed, so they update by themselves when pages are added or removed. If you type page numbers by hand they will be wrong as soon as the document changes.

Watch out

Never type a page number or a date of printing by hand in a footer; insert the field so it stays correct.

Check what you just learned

1. Why insert a page number field instead of typing it?
  • Fields look better
  • It is shorter
  • It updates automatically (correct)
  • It is bold

A field changes when pages are added or removed.

Key terms: flip and sort

Style
A named set of formatting
Heading 1
The top-level heading style
Margin
The empty border around a page
Header
Repeating area at the top of each page
Footer
Repeating area at the bottom of each page
Field
Content that updates itself, such as a page number
keyPoints: Headers and footers repeat on every page.
Page numbers must be fields, not typed numbers.

modules.title: Tables and layout
modules.summary: Use tables, pictures and breaks to line up information and control where things land.
modules.outcome: You can build and format a table, place pictures with a caption and alternative text, and use page and section breaks.
modules.intro: When information has two dimensions, such as days and subjects or items and prices, a table lines it up better than any amount of spaces. This module also covers pictures and breaks, the other tools that control layout.

topics.title: Building a table
topics.html:
Choose Insert, Table and pick the number of columns and rows. Click a cell to type. Tab moves to the next cell; pressing Tab in the last cell adds a new row.

Table vocabulary
TermMeaning
RowA horizontal line of cells
ColumnA vertical line of cells
CellOne box where a row and a column meet
Header rowThe first row that names each column
MergeJoining cells into one
Worked example

A study timetable

A group needs a timetable for Monday to Friday with morning and afternoon subjects.

  1. Insert a table with 6 rows and 3 columns.
  2. The first row holds Day, Morning, Afternoon.
  3. Fill each day in the first column and the subjects across.

Answer. Rows are days, columns are time slots, and the header row labels them.

Tip

Keep tables simple. If you need many merged cells, a spreadsheet may be the better tool.

Check what you just learned

1. Which key moves to the next table cell?
  • Enter
  • F2
  • Esc
  • Tab (correct)

Tab moves right; at the end it adds a row.

2. What does the header row do?
  • Names each column (correct)
  • Holds the totals
  • Hides the table
  • Colours the cells

It labels the columns.
keyPoints: Rows go across, columns go down.
Tab moves to the next cell and adds rows.
The header row names the columns.

topics.title: Making a table readable
topics.html:
Habits of a readable table

  1. Make the header row bold.
  2. Align numbers to the right and text to the left.
  3. Use light borders, and shading only to help the eye.
  4. Keep the same units in each column (put them in the heading).
  5. Leave some padding so text does not touch the lines.
Same data, two versions
PoorBetter
No header, centred numbers, heavy bordersBold header, right-aligned numbers, light lines
Units repeated in every cellUnit in the column heading
Watch out

Do not use a table just to push text across a page. If the content is not data, use paragraphs and headings.

Check what you just learned

1. Where do units belong in a table of prices?
  • In every cell
  • In the column heading (correct)
  • Nowhere
  • In the footer

Putting units in the heading keeps cells clean.
keyPoints: Bold header, right-aligned numbers, light borders.
Put units in headings.

topics.title: Pictures, captions and breaks
topics.html:
A picture should earn its place: it should show something words cannot say quickly. Insert it, size it so it fits within the margins, and add a caption that says what it shows. Add alternative text, a short description for people who cannot see the image.

Breaks
BreakUse for
Page breakStart a new page here (a chapter, a table)
Section breakChange the page layout, such as portrait to landscape
Column breakMove text to the next column
Tip

Select a picture and use its alt text option. A good description is one short sentence: 'Bar chart showing most students walk to school.'

Common mistakes

  • Stretching a picture out of proportion; drag a corner handle instead of a side handle.
  • Leaving pictures without captions or alt text.

Check what you just learned

1. What is alternative text for?
  • Decoration
  • Bolding it
  • Describing a picture for people who cannot see it (correct)
  • Moving it

Alt text tells the reader what the image shows.

Key terms: flip and sort

Table
Rows and columns of cells
Header row
The row that names the columns
Merge
Join cells together
Caption
A short line explaining a picture or table
Alt text
A text description of an image
Page break
Starts a new page at a chosen point
keyPoints: Add captions and alt text to pictures.
Use page breaks, not blank lines, to start a new page.

options: Digits line up for easy comparison

Stretching a picture from the side handle will:

modules.title: Professional documents
modules.summary: Write letters, résumés, reports and minutes that look right and read clearly.
modules.outcome: You can lay out a formal letter, a one-page résumé, a short report and meeting minutes, and explain why each is built the way it is.
modules.intro: Formal documents follow conventions so the reader knows where to look. Learn the layout of each type once and you will be able to produce a good one quickly.

topics.title: Formal letters and emails
topics.html:
Greeting and closing pairs
GreetingClosing
Dear Ms Rao,Yours sincerely,
Dear Sir or Madam,Yours faithfully,
Dear Principal,Yours sincerely,

Writing well

  1. Say why you are writing in the first sentence.
  2. One idea per paragraph, three to five sentences each.
  3. Be polite and specific: give dates, amounts and names.
  4. Thank the reader and say what happens next.
Worked example

Make a request clearly

A student asks to borrow the hall.

  1. First sentence: I would like to request the school hall on Friday 14 March from 4 pm to 6 pm.
  2. Second paragraph: the purpose, a rehearsal for the annual day.
  3. Close: thank you and an offer to answer questions.

Answer. A formal request names exactly what you want, when, and why.

Check what you just learned

1. A letter starting Dear Sir or Madam normally ends with:
  • Yours sincerely
  • Cheers
  • Best wishes
  • Yours faithfully (correct)

Yours faithfully pairs with Dear Sir or Madam.

2. Where should you state why you are writing?
  • In the first sentence (correct)
  • At the end
  • In the footer
  • Never

Readers want the purpose at once.
keyPoints: Date, greeting, purpose, details, closing.
Dear Name closes with Yours sincerely; Dear Sir or Madam closes with Yours faithfully.

topics.title: Résumés and cover letters
topics.html:
A résumé (or CV) is a one-page summary of who you are and what you can do. Recruiters scan it in seconds, so it must be easy to skim.

Sections of a student résumé
SectionWhat to include
Name and contactName, email and phone; city is enough
SummaryTwo sentences: who you are and what you want
SkillsFour to eight relevant skills as a list
EducationSchool or college, year and results
Projects or experienceWhat you did and what happened, with numbers where possible
Tip

Start achievement lines with a verb and add a number: Organised a book fair for 200 students.

Common mistakes

  • Writing a paragraph about yourself instead of short lines.
  • Using several fonts or colours.
  • Leaving out contact details or using an unprofessional email address.

Check what you just learned

1. Which line is best on a résumé?
  • I am hard working
  • Organised a book fair for 200 students (correct)
  • Many skills
  • Good with computers

Specific, verb-led lines with numbers are strongest.
keyPoints: One page, scannable sections, verbs and numbers.
Consistent formatting and a professional email address.

topics.title: Reports and meeting minutes
topics.html:
Put the conclusion first. Busy readers may read only the summary, so it must say what you found and what you recommend. Then give the evidence in tables, lists and short paragraphs.

Meeting minutes
PartContent
HeadingMeeting name and date
AttendeesWho was there and who sent apologies
DecisionsWhat was agreed, numbered
ActionsTask, owner and deadline in a table
Tip

Write minutes the same day, while you remember what was said. Record decisions and actions, not every word.

Check what you just learned

1. What should minutes mainly record?
  • Every word spoken
  • Jokes
  • Decisions and actions (correct)
  • Only names

Minutes are a record of decisions and actions.

2. In a short report the summary comes:
  • Last
  • Nowhere
  • In the footer
  • First (correct)

The summary comes first.

Key terms: flip and sort

Letter closing
Yours sincerely or Yours faithfully
Résumé
A one-page summary of skills and experience
Summary
The short overview at the start of a report
Minutes
A record of decisions and actions from a meeting
Action item
A task with an owner
keyPoints: Reports lead with the summary and recommendation.
Minutes record decisions and actions with owners.

modules.title: Review, collaborate and finish
modules.summary: Proofread, use track changes and comments, make documents accessible and export them safely.
modules.outcome: You can check a document for errors, review someone else's work, make a document accessible and share it in the right form.
modules.intro: Most mistakes are found by checking, not by writing. This final module covers the tools for proofreading, working with other people and delivering a finished document that everyone can read.

topics.title: Proofreading and readability
topics.html:
Spell check finds words that are not in the dictionary, but it cannot find the wrong word spelled correctly: their and there, form and from. Read your work aloud, or after a break, to catch those.

A proofreading routine

  1. Run the spelling and grammar check.
  2. Read slowly, out loud, one paragraph at a time.
  3. Check names, numbers, dates and headings twice.
  4. Look at the layout: consistent fonts, spacing and alignment.
  5. Ask someone else to read it.
Common word mix-ups
WrongRightTip
recievereceivei before e except after c
their / there / they'rechoose by meaningtheir = owned by them; there = a place; they're = they are
its / it'sits = belonging; it's = it isTry expanding it's to it is
Tip

Aim for short sentences. If a sentence needs two breaths when read aloud, split it.

Check what you just learned

1. Which error can a spell checker miss?
  • Using form instead of from (correct)
  • recieve
  • xyzzy
  • adn

Both words are real, so the spell checker does not object.
keyPoints: Spell check misses correct words in the wrong place.
Reading aloud and a second reader find the rest.

topics.title: Track changes and comments
topics.html:
Track changes records every edit as a suggestion instead of changing the text directly. The author can accept or reject each one. Comments are notes in the margin attached to a piece of text.

Good review manners

  • Say why in a comment, not just what.
  • Be kind and specific: suggest an alternative.
  • Resolve a comment when it is dealt with.
  • Turn off track changes before sending the final version.
Watch out

Always check that no tracked changes or comments remain before you send a final document. Hidden suggestions can embarrass you.

Check what you just learned

1. What does Track changes do?
  • Deletes text
  • Records edits as suggestions (correct)
  • Saves the file
  • Counts words

It shows who changed what and lets the author decide.
keyPoints: Track changes shows every edit as a suggestion.
Accept or reject each change; clear everything before sending.

topics.title: Accessibility, security and sharing
topics.html:
Making a document accessible

  1. Use real heading styles in order.
  2. Write meaningful link text, not click here.
  3. Add alt text to pictures.
  4. Choose strong contrast and a readable size.
  5. Do not use colour as the only signal.
Sharing choices
GoalChoose
People will edit itShare the DOCX or an online document with edit access
People should only read itExport a PDF or share a view-only link
Sensitive contentPassword protect and share only with the people who need it

Before you share, check the document properties for your name and any old titles, and remove hidden comments. Keep an unedited original, and name the final version clearly.

Tip

Run the built-in accessibility checker if your program has one. It lists problems such as missing alt text.

Check what you just learned

1. Which link text is best?
  • Click here
  • Link
  • Read the school safety policy (correct)
  • Here

Link text should make sense alone.

2. To stop people editing a finished file you can:
  • Email the DOCX
  • Use a bigger font
  • Add more colour
  • Send a PDF (correct)

PDF fixes the content.

Key terms: flip and sort

Proofreading
Checking a document for errors
Track changes
Records edits as suggestions
Comment
A note in the margin
Alt text
A description of an image
Contrast
Difference between text and background colour
keyPoints: Accessible documents use real headings, alt text and good contrast.
Share a PDF or view-only link when people should not edit.
